newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly firmer, volume low.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly firmer, volume low.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly higher Tuesday, but volume remained low and historical volatilities continued to drift back in most of the complex.

"Neither volume, nor volatility nor lease rates have responded much lately, despite whispers of more central bank gold sales, or the jump in the dollar again today," Chase Manhattan New York managing director Dinsa Mehta said.
COMEX June gold ended up $0.20 at $351.20 an ounce after trading from $350.50 to $352.30, within the range of $348.30 to $358.00 during the past month.

Daily momentum oscillators remain neutral, while 20-day historical volatility has drifted back below 10 percent for the first time since January, but the June contract's five day (weekly) moving average remains below both its 21-day (monthly) and 55-day (quarterly) average, analysts said.

Estimated volume for COMEX gold was only 17,000 contracts Tuesday, while open interest in COMEX gold fell a further 2,703 lots Monday to 147,494 contracts, the lowest level in over a year, reflecting the fall in volatility and lack of direction, traders said.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted at $348.30/80 compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix of $349.10 and Monday's New York close of $348.50/$349.00.
Short-term implied lease rates remained low, with the one month rate still below 1.00 percent, suggesting there was little interest in financing speculative short positions, analysts said.
However, the ongoing rise in U.S. bill and bond interest rates this week was slightly bearish for gold, analysts said.

"With the Fed funds at 5.5 percent, the real return on money in the U.S. is around 2.75 percent and that rate of real return should help to keep the dollar strong against other currencies and that is not a good thing for gold offtake because gold becomes more expensive in local currency terms," Merrill Lynch analyst Ted Arnold said.
"A strong dollar and high U.S. real interest rates encourage more producer forward selling particularly on prices spikes or rallies," he said.
COMEX May silver ended down 1.0 cent at $4.785 after trading from $4.825 to $4.750.

The May contract has been recovering from last week's oversold condition, after seeing a contract low last Thursday at $4.655, but the contract's five-day average remains below both its 21-day and 55-day average.
The spot gold/silver ratio was little changed around 72.86, after recovering in the past two months from a 22-month low at 65.6.
Platinum group metals again looked the most promising in the complex analysts said, with the focus still on the lack of Russian exports this year.
"The platinum group looks like it may provide some direction again, but so far the rest of the complex hasn't responded," FIMAT New York trader John Tyree said.
NYMEX July platinum ended up $0.80 at $369.50, with the NYMEX October platinum/COMEX October gold spread up to $14.60 from a two-month low of $10.20 posted Monday.

NYMEX June palladium gained $1.35 to $153.75 after seeing a four-week intraday high of $157.50, with one-month lease rates reported to be up to six percent in Tokyo as demand for palladium from Swiss entrepot stocks rises.
Earlier this week, Russian officials said there would be no exports of Russian palladium to Japan in April and possibly none in May, while overall 1997 exports would be much lower.
Russia supplies about 60 percent of the world's palladium while Japan consumes about 40 percent of the metal in automotive and electronic applications.
